fields.why: The claims rest on rates and percentages; the median age of decedents describes the cases rather than an outcome. A's 'continuous' fits the letter of the definition (medians of a measured quantity), so both values are defensible.

'however, the rate ... among blacks was more than twice the rate of whites' is a computed relative contrast with a disparity framing, so the side-by-side cap does not apply. Level 2 is defensible only if 'interpreted' requires more than the closing 'culturally appropriate for the highest risk populations' line.
This follows the equity_level verdict of 3.
The brief says to record sex always; the text has '115 (84%) occurred among males' (descriptor). A left it out.

The Editorial Note names the narrow scope of state laws ('regulations pertaining to alcohol use focus only on boat operators'). That is a political determinant recorded even below level 4, though it explains overall risk, not the racial gap.

brief_issues: 'Interpreted' at level 3 is undefined: does a single 'however ... more than twice' sentence plus a generic call for culturally appropriate prevention count? The brief should also say whether descriptive medians of case characteristics (age) count as a 'continuous' outcome.
